note: Close's docs say API keys use HTTP Basic client side authentication. Basic is the transport for the key, not a separate login method, so the auth method is api_key plus oauth2.
Help Scout has no free plan, but a developer can get API access during the 15-day Standard or Plus trial, which is the free_trial tier as defined in the brief. Consistent with Zendesk and Freshdesk.
The MCP registry lists third-party Gladly servers. Gladly publishes none, so the right value is community, not none.
Pumble's MCP guide requires the user and bot tokens issued when an app is installed, which fits bearer_token as defined (a token issued some other way), alongside the API key addon.
WhatsApp's multi-tenant path is Embedded Signup, which uses Facebook Login (OAuth). System-user tokens cover only a business's own account, so oauth2 belongs in the list.

Aircall customers can create Basic-auth API keys on their own account without any partner step. A toolkit that takes customer-supplied keys is buildable; only the OAuth path needs the Technology Partner Program.
Partner programme blocks the OAuth path; a paid plan may gate the key path (the plan floor comes only from the pricing page). Both readings are supported.
Magento Open Source is free and self-hosted; Adobe Commerce is licensed. The docs cover both editions.
NMI publishes an official MCP server, but no Paygent-branded server was found and the Paygent Connect product could not be matched. Official applies to NMI only.
Intuit documents GraphQL APIs for QuickBooks Online (developer.intuit.com, Develop your app with the GraphQL API), so graphql belongs in the list.
The public Gemini Notebook API is free in preview for personal Google accounts; the separate Enterprise API needs a licence. Both exist.
The pass 2 evidence for rpc is the MCP server's JSON-RPC transport, which is the MCP wire format and not the API style. The API itself is REST.
A licence is needed for the Enterprise API and the public API is narrow. Both readings are supported.
